title: On‑Call Rapid Investigation Cheatsheet — Serving Runtime
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose

This one-page cheatsheet is designed for first responders on the serving-runtime oncall rotation. It emphasizes fast, high-confidence checks to determine whether a user-visible degradation is: 1) a routing/capacity incident, 2) a kernel or accelerator-level regression, 3) a model/quantization quality issue, or 4) a networking/storage problem. Use this as the initial investigation path to minimize mean time to mitigation (MTTM).

When to use

- Any alert with SLO impact: 95th/99th token latency breach, error rate spike > 1% absolute, or token cost anomaly.
- Customer-reported failures affecting multiple tenants or a Dedicated pool.
- Sudden increase in timeouts, streaming truncations, or model-variant fallbacks.

Quick triage checklist (1–10 minutes)

1) Validate user-facing signal
   - Confirm whether the symptom is global or cohort-specific (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
   - Check primary dashboards: "Routes SLO Overview" and "Token Latency by Model Variant" for immediate spikes.

2) Confirm impact scope
   - Isolated to one region? One model? One capacity pool?
   - Look at per-route and per-tenant panels. If only one tenant -> follow customer escalation playbook.

3) Surface network and infra alarms
   - Fast check on infra alerts: node reboots, GPU watchdogs, NVLink errors, cloud network flaps.
   - If there are node-level alerts, mark as likely infra and contact infra-sre.

4) Kernel / scheduling symptoms
   - Identify: concurrent kernel queue growth, long queue times, repeated preemption events.
   - If kernel queue depth correlates with latency, apply admission-control throttle (see Temporary Mitigation).

5) Model & quantization fallbacks
   - Check model swap events and fallback logs: "model_swap_reason" and "quantize_fallback" tags in traces.
   - Correlate recent deployments/rollouts to timing of incident.

6) Caching and KV warmup
   - Look for high miss rates on KV cache and cold-start traces. If a mass warmup is in progress, expect transient latency as caches populate.

Immediate data sources (quick links)

- Observability dashboards: /dashboards/runtime/routes-slo-overview, /dashboards/runtime/kernel-queue, /dashboards/runtime/kvcache-hitrate
- Tracing: Jaeger/Tempo -> Search by trace tags: service=runtime, event=dispatch|kernel|evict, model=<name>
- Logs: central-log (fluentd) queries: "level>=WARN AND (kernel OR eviction OR model_swap)" within last 15m
- Metric queries (Graphite/Prometheus):
  - runtime_dispatch_queue_length{pool="<pool>"}
  - kernel_execution_time_seconds{kernel="attention"}
  - kvcache_hit_rate{shard="*"}
  - per_route_error_rate{route="<route>"}

Fast instrumentation queries (copy-paste)

- Prometheus: max_over_time(runtime_dispatch_queue_length[5m]) > 100 -> indicates queue saturation
- Prometheus: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(kernel_execution_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le,kernel))
- Fluentd (CLI): 
  curl -s "https://logs.redwood.internal/query?q=level%3D%3DWARN%20AND%20(kernel%20OR%20evict%20OR%20model_swap)&from=-15m" | jq -r '.results[] | .message'

Temporary mitigations (safe, quick)

- Canary route diversion: divert 50% of traffic from affected route to the stable model-variant for 10m. Use console -> Routing -> Temporary divert.
- Admission throttles: apply soft admission limit on the afflicted pool to target queue depth <= 50. Command (operator CLI):
  rwdctl pool throttle set --pool-id <pool> --max-queue 50 --reason "oncall-mitigation"
- Increase autoscale burst for Dedicated pool (if allowed by contract) to blunt sudden throughput surges.
- Retry policy tweak: temporarily set per-request client retry to linear backoff 200ms x 3 to reduce concurrent pressure.

When to escalate

- Escalate to Eng-SRE within 10 minutes if any of: GPU watchdogs present, node OOMs, NVLink bit errors, or >2% sustained 5m SLO breach.
- Escalate to Serving Runtime Kernel team if kernel queue growth remains after admission throttles or if kernel execution time 99th increases by >2x.
- Escalate to Model Onboarding if model fallback/quality regressions coincide with a new model rollout.

Escalation contacts (fast list)

- Eng-SRE Pager: +1-555-0100 (pager) / #eng-sre-oncall
- Serving Runtime Kernel team: @kernel-oncall (Slack) / email kernel-oncall@redwood.ai
- Model Onboarding: @model-oncall / model-oncall@redwood.ai

Investigation play (30–90 minutes)

1) Capture canonical traces: use sampling label "oncall-rapid" and capture 200 traces across affected routes.
2) Run head-to-head microbenchmarks for suspect model-variant on a sandbox node to reproduce elevated kernel exec times. Use the local perf harness:
   ./perf/harness/run_bench --model <model> --sequence 512 --batch 1 --profile
3) If KV miss rate high: run kvcache-prefetch for top 10 prefixes for the route:
   rwdctl kvcache prefetch --route <route> --prefix-file top_prefixes.txt
4) If networking suspected: correlate pod/node network metrics (qdisc drops, retransmits) and cross-check cloud VPC flow logs.

Post-incident steps (ownership and timeline)

- Owner: first responder creates incident ticket and assigns to kernel or infra with summary, key traces, metric snapshots, and mitigation steps taken.
- Within 48 hours: postmortem draft with timeline, root cause hypothesis, and proposed corrective actions.
- Within 7 days: implement one low-effort fix (config, throttle change, or alert tuning).

Quick reference table: SLO thresholds and first responder targets

| Signal | SLO | First-responder target | Typical owner |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 95th token latency (global) | <= 400ms | Acknowledge in 5m, mitigate in 30m | Eng-SRE / Runtime |
| 99th token latency (route) | <= 800ms | Acknowledge in 5m, mitigate in 60m | Runtime Kernel |
| Error rate (per-route) | <= 0.5% | Acknowledge in 5m, mitigate in 30m | Runtime / CS |
| KV cache hit-rate | >= 95% | Identify warmup in 10m | Runtime Ops |

Appendix: Useful snippets and dashboards

- Example trace tags to search:
  - span.tags: {"runtime.phase": "dispatch"}, {"kernel.name":"matmul"}, {"model.variant":"v2-quant"}
- Console actions (UI):
  1. Routing -> Route Health -> Open incident divert
  2. Pools -> Select pool -> Throttles & Autoscale -> Apply temporary change
- Local helper scripts (location): /ops/oncall-scripts/fast_summaries.sh

FAQ / gotchas

- "Why did admission throttle not reduce latency?" -> If kernel execution is the dominant contributor (not queueing), throttling won't help; check kernel_execution_time.
- "We see many model_swap events but no deploys" -> Check quantization autoswitch policy and per-tenant override config.

Owners and maintenance

- Primary owner: Serving Runtime Oncall rotation (team wiki -> rotation calendar).
- Document maintainer: Aisha Patel (serving-runtime-observability team). Please update this cheatsheet after any change to Route SLOs, dispatch instrumentation, or oncall runbook.

Revision history

- 2023-11-15: Initial draft (A. Patel).
- 2024-06-18: Added KV-prefetch quick step and Prometheus queries (D. Morales).
- 2024-12-05: Updated escalation thresholds and automation commands (P. Shah).
